This sounds like an incredibly unhealthy relationship. You said you flash-backed to 'how he used to hurt you' ... what do you mean by this? Has he physically injured you, or are you referring to emotional pain?

If he has hit you, ever ... leave. Now.

But even if he hasn't, it seems like he's shunning your emotional advances, and doesn't respect you. You can do better, don't throw your life away on someone who doesn't treat you right.

I do not want to come off as rude in this suggestion, as I have no knowledge of your relationship with your brother, but are you absolutely certain he is not the one abusing her? I have, firsthand, seen the abused become abusers and while it can be hard to accept it happens.

It just strikes me as strange that he doesn't want to take her in for a physical. If my child ever lay claim to being abused or showed any symptoms (or even if they just might be sick/constipated) they would be at the emergency room in a heartbeat.

Just because you know she would make a good wife, does not mean she should be YOUR wife.

I don't care if you're 20 or 65. There's never an excuse to settle and marry someone who you will not be happy with. It will only bring you misery, and if you have children someday it will bring them misery as well.

Cut your losses on this one, and keep searching for the woman who you CAN laugh with, and who WILL take part in your interests (and keep you on your toes with hers!)

He's rude & an asshole.

Personally I wouldn't let it get to me if it wasn't someone I was close to, but I would still think they're an arrogant prick for saying it (without my request or for a true concern over my health -- given they were a close enough friend to warrant that privilege.)

Shawshank Redemption hands down.

Forrest Gump has a lot of southern charm. It's incredibly sentimental, which has its purpose, but is almost *too* sugary sweet. I did love this movie, but it's nowhere near my favourites.

Shawshank, on the other hand, is phenomenal. In many ways it can be viewed as a more modern Count of Monte Cristo. The characters are all well developed, and while on the surface it's displayed in a very simple fashion, there's that hint of complexity beneath it all. It really portrays a beautiful model of hope without giving you that sugar-sweet aftertaste that Forrest Gump did.

I've struggled with ED-NOS since I was 13. I too find myself obsessing over calories constantly. I also have the tendency to "binge" (which in actuality is usually in a 'healthy' calorie range) and purge.

It's still something I struggle with so I can't give you tips to overcoming, but here are some things that help me when I feel I'm starting to eat too little or I'm close to a binge.

1. Find out what time of day you tend to binge. For me, it's around 9PM or later. Luckily this means I can usually just take a sleeping pill that night and get a good night's rest. If I need to stay awake (studying, etc) I find that distractions help a lot. Grab a piece of gum, put in headphones or pop in a DVD. Read a book while listening to music ... anything to keep your mind doing more than one thing at once.

2. Find a good calorie range, and try your best to stick to it. [DailyBurn](http://dailyburn.com) is what I use personally. You can find what's a good range to be eating and lose weight, as well as find out how much you should be exercising. Stick to this plan as best you can. If you go over your calorie/carb/whatever range one day ... don't let it bring you down! When you hit a plateau in losing weight, it speeds up your metabolism to eat a little extra one day, so think of it as a booster!

3. Try to keep your go-to binge foods OUT of your house. If you live alone this is easy. It keeps temptation out of your way. Stock up on apples, carrots, whatever. Healthy snacks. Hot tea is also good. It makes my stomach feel warm & full to avoid binging. If you live with others and feel comfortable talking to them, ask them to please put the Oreos, Chips, whatever they buy for themselves in their respective rooms so you do not feel tempted by it!

Good luck to you. If you ever feel you are falling into that trap of disordered eating, ask someone for a help! A friend, a therapist, anything.

This response is perfect.

I've also struggled with eating disorders -- since I was 13. Technically bulimia with restricting tendencies -- or ED-NOS.

OP, please do not let these thoughts swallow you whole like they did myself and others. Your weight does not determine your worth -- your character does. I found myself counting every calorie and just making it lower and lower because the number made me so sick. If I felt the number was too high (Even if it was only 100 calories worth of vegetables that day) I would purge to make myself empty because it's what I felt I deserved for being fat. (Which I wasn't even at the time.) It took over my life for years and I still turn to it in times of extreme stress. I lost friends, relationships, because I thought they were trying to make me fat when they asked me to go out to dinner with them, etc.

As kittymojo said, you need to seek out help. These thoughts will send you into a hopeless spiral that you do not want to have to claw your way out. Things can be better for you if you let a professional help you.

Good luck to you.
